def-intersection-volume-conservative-rem:
## Definition

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable domain of finite positive measure. Let $\mathcal S=(S_i)_{i=1}^m$ and $\mathcal T=(T_j)_{j=1}^n$ be finite measurable partitions of $\Omega$ up to null sets, with disjoint interiors modulo null sets and positive cell volumes. Define exact overlap weights $w_{ji}=|T_j\cap S_i|$. For source constants $v_i$, the intersection-volume remap is the target piecewise-constant field $Rv$ whose value on $T_j$ is $ (Rv)_j=|T_j|^{-1}\sum_i w_{ji}v_i$. All weights are exact measures; an approximate clipping weight is not silently substituted.
def-isoparametric-curved-cell-map:
## Definition

Fix a reference matching affine simplicial mesh as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. An admissible curved cell is the image of a closed reference simplex $\widehat K$ under a map $F_K\in C^2(\widehat K;\mathbb R^d)$ that extends to a diffeomorphism on a neighborhood, is orientation preserving, and satisfies $0<j_0\le J_K:=\det DF_K\le j_1$ and $\|DF_K\|+\|(DF_K)^{-1}\|+\|D^2F_K\|\le C_F$. The physical cells have disjoint interiors, cover the domain up to their shared facets, and maps agree on each common reference facet under the prescribed affine facet identification. Define the volume metric $G_K=DF_K^TDF_K$, volume factor $J_K=\sqrt{\det G_K}$, and for a reference facet parametrization $\widehat f$ the surface metric $G_{K,\widehat f}=D(F_K\circ\widehat f)^TD(F_K\circ\widehat f)$ and surface factor $\sqrt{\det G_{K,\widehat f}}$. The positive-Jacobian lower bound is the admissibility certificate; it is not inferred from a drawing or from Delaunay quality.
lem-h2-zero-boundary-p1-interpolant-conf:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let
$\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ have a finite matching affine triangular mesh, and let
$u\in H^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\cap H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. On each triangle
take the unique continuous representative of the restriction of $u$. These
representatives give one well-defined value at every mesh vertex. The global
nodal P1 interpolant $I_hu$, affine on each triangle and equal to these values
at its vertices, is continuous, has zero trace on every boundary edge, and
belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$.
def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation:
## Definition

Let $\widehat\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded reference domain and let $\Phi,\Phi_h:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\mathbb R^d$ be cellwise $C^2$ admissible maps with matching traces, positive Jacobians, and common image topology. The exact and approximate domains are $\Omega=\Phi(\widehat\Omega)$ and $\Omega_h=\Phi_h(\widehat\Omega)$. Define $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega)}$ and $e_1=\|D\Phi-D\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega;op)}$. A geometry approximation claim must separately state bounds on $e_0,e_1$, both Jacobian lower bounds, and boundary-trace compatibility; none follows from the word “isoparametric.”
lem-curved-p1-interpolation-scaling:
## Statement

Assume AC and Countable Choice. In dimension two let $K=\Psi(\widetilde K)$, where $\widetilde K$ is a shape-regular affine triangle of diameter comparable to $h_K$, and $\Psi$ extends to a $C^2$ diffeomorphism on a neighborhood of $\overline{\widetilde K}$. Assume $\|D\Psi\|_\infty+\|D\Psi^{-1}\|_\infty+\|D^2\Psi\|_\infty+\|J_\Psi^{-1}\|_\infty$ are uniformly bounded. Let $v$ denote its continuous representative and set $I_Kv=(I_{\widetilde K}(v\circ\Psi))\circ\Psi^{-1}$, the mapped nodal P1 interpolant. For $v\in H^2(K)$, $\|v-I_Kv\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K^2\|v\|_{H^2(K)}$ and $|v-I_Kv|_{H^1(K)}\le C h_K\|v\|_{H^2(K)}$, with $C$ uniform over the family.
thm-overlap-remap-l2-projection-conserva:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Under the finite partition hypotheses of [[def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping]], let $P_0(\mathcal T)$ be the target cellwise-constant subspace of $L^2(\Omega)$. For every source piecewise-constant $v$, $Rv$ is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection of $v$ onto $P_0(\mathcal T)$, hence $\|Rv\|_2\le\|v\|_2$. It preserves total mass, $\int_\Omega Rv=\int_\Omega v$, and if all $v_i\ge0$ then every target value $(Rv)_j\ge0$.
lem-curved-boundary-lift-residual:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ be covered by a finite matching cell mesh, and let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be continuous geometry maps whose cellwise $C^1$ derivatives satisfy $\|D\Phi\|_\infty+\|D\Phi_h\|_\infty\le M$, $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_\infty$, and $e_1=\|D\Phi-D\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty;op}$. Let $G$ be a scalar physical boundary lift on an open convex neighborhood containing both images and every segment joining corresponding image points, with $\|DG\|_\infty\le L_1$ and $\|D^2G\|_\infty\le L_2$. Define the piecewise pullback gradients by $
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi)=D\Phi^T
abla G(\Phi)$ and $
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi_h)=D\Phi_h^T
abla G(\Phi_h)$, and set
$$\ell_{\partial,h}(w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega} ig(
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi)-
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi_h) ig)\cdot
abla w,\qquad w\in H^1_0(\widehat\Omega).$$
With the $H^1$ dual norm, $\|\ell_{\partial,h}\|_{(H^1_0)^*}\le 2(L_1e_1+ML_2e_0)$. Thus the geometry-induced boundary-lift contribution to the Strang load defect is $O(e_0+e_1)$.
lem-isoparametric-cofactor-normal-pertur:
## Statement

Let $A=D\Phi$ and $A_h=D\Phi_h$ be orientation-preserving cell-map derivatives with $\det A,\det A_h\ge j_*>0$, $\|A\|_{op},\|A_h\|_{op}\le M$, and $\|A-A_h\|_{op}\le e_1$. For every unit reference-facet normal $\widehat n$, define the surface Jacobians $J_\Gamma(A)=\|\operatorname{cof}(A)\widehat n\|$, $J_\Gamma(A_h)=\|\operatorname{cof}(A_h)\widehat n\|$, and mapped unit normals $n_\Gamma(A)=\operatorname{cof}(A)\widehat n/J_\Gamma(A)$ and $n_\Gamma(A_h)=\operatorname{cof}(A_h)\widehat n/J_\Gamma(A_h)$. Then
$$\|\operatorname{cof}(A)-\operatorname{cof}(A_h)\|_{op}+|J_\Gamma(A)-J_\Gamma(A_h)|+|n_\Gamma(A)-n_\Gamma(A_h)|\le C(d,M,j_*)e_1.$$
The surface Jacobian agrees with the Gram-metric factor in [[def-isoparametric-curved-cell-map]].
lem-isoparametric-laplace-tensor-defect:
## Statement

Let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be the orientation-preserving maps of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]], with $J,J_h\ge j_*>0$ and $\|D\Phi\|_\infty+\|D\Phi_h\|_\infty\le M$. Set $B=J D\Phi^{-1}D\Phi^{-T}$ and $B_h=J_hD\Phi_h^{-1}D\Phi_h^{-T}$. Then $\|B-B_h\|_\infty\le C e_1$, where $C$ depends only on $d,j_*,M$. Consequently $|\int_{\widehat\Omega}
abla v^T(B-B_h)
abla w|\le C e_1\|
abla v\|_2\|
abla w\|_2$ for $v,w\in H^1(\widehat\Omega)$.
lem-parabolic-domain-map-approximation:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=[-1,1]^2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a matching shape-regular affine triangulation, and put $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$. Let $I_h$ be the vertexwise P1 interpolant and $\Phi_h(x,y)=(x,y+I_h(x^2/4))$. In the notation of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]], there is a constant $C$ depending only on the shape-regularity bound such that $e_0\le Ch^2$ and $e_1\le Ch$. For sufficiently small $h$, $\det D\Phi_h\ge1/2$, and $\Phi_h$ is globally one-to-one on the square. The exact map has $\det D\Phi=1$ and a global inverse $(X,Y)\mapsto(X,Y-X^2/4)$.
thm-overlap-remap-error-from-approximati:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega$ be bounded, let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be the geometry maps of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]] and assume each is a global orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism from $\widehat\Omega$ onto its image, with $J_h\le J^*$ and $u$ is $L_u$-Lipschitz on the union of their images. On $\Omega_h=\Phi_h(\widehat\Omega)$ let $\mathcal S,\mathcal T$ be finite positive-volume partitions and let $v_S$ be source-piecewise-constant data with finite $L^2$ error. Assume the exact target projection error below is finite. Define $P_Tq$ on each target cell by its exact cell average, $\eta_S=\|u-v_S\|_{L^2(\Omega_h)}$, and $\eta_T=\|u-P_Tu\|_{L^2(\Omega_h)}$. If $R$ is the exact overlap remap, then\n$$\|u\circ\Phi-(Rv_S)\circ\Phi_h\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega,J_h)}\le L_u e_0\sqrt{J^*|\widehat\Omega|}+\eta_S+\eta_T,$$\nwhere $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_\infty$ and $\|z\|_{L^2(\widehat\Omega,J_h)}^2=\int_{\widehat\Omega}|z|^2J_h$.
lem-curved-nvb-closure-preserves-matchin:
## Statement

Let a compatible labeled reference triangulation be refined by recursive reference-edge closure as in [[alg-dorfler-marking-and-conforming-nvb-refinement]]. The closure terminates in a matching conforming affine descendant. If every cell is mapped through one common injective geometry map whose traces agree on common reference facets, the resulting curved cells also have matching interfaces.
thm-curved-isoparametric-strang-error-bo:
## Statement
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=(-1,1)^2$, let $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$, and let $\Phi_h$ be its continuous piecewise-affine nodal interpolant on a shape-regular matching triangular mesh with maximum diameter $h\le1$, small enough that $J_h=\det D\Phi_h\ge1/2$ as in [[lem-parabolic-domain-map-approximation]]. Put $J=\det D\Phi$ and define the pulled-back Laplace tensors $$B=J D\Phi^{-1}D\Phi^{-T},\qquad B_h=J_hD\Phi_h^{-1}D\Phi_h^{-T}.$$ On $V=H^1_0(\widehat\Omega)$ set $$a(v,w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega}
abla v^TB
abla w,\qquad a_h(v,w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega}
abla v^TB_h
abla w.$$ Let $V_h$ be the finite-dimensional space of continuous functions on $\overline{\widehat\Omega}$ that are affine on each triangle and vanish on $\partial\widehat\Omega$, viewed as a subspace of $V$. Suppose $a$ and $a_h$ are uniformly bounded and coercive on $V$ and $V_h$, respectively, with constants independent of $h$, $F\in V^*$ and $F_h\in V_h^*$ are bounded, $u\in H^2(\widehat\Omega)\cap V$ is real-valued and satisfies $a(u,w)=F(w)$ for every $w\in V$, and $u_h\in V_h$ satisfies $a_h(u_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$.

If a common physical boundary lift $G\in C^2$ with bounded first and second derivatives on a convex neighborhood of the two geometry images is used, let $\ell_{\partial,h}$ be its pulled-back residual from [[lem-curved-boundary-lift-residual]] and set $\epsilon_{\partial,h}=\|\ell_{\partial,h}\|_{V^*}$. Assume the load difference on $V_h$ splits as $$ (F-F_h)|_{V_h}=L_{\mathrm{bulk},h}+\ell_{\partial,h}|_{V_h},\qquad \|L_{\mathrm{bulk},h}\|_{V_h^*}\le\epsilon_{F,h}^{\mathrm{bulk}},\qquad \epsilon_{F,h}^{\mathrm{bulk}}\ge0.$$ Here the $V^*$ and $V_h^*$ norms are induced by the $H^1$ norm. If no lift is used, set $\ell_{\partial,h}=0$ and take the same bound for the full load difference. Then $$\|u-u_h\|_{H^1(\widehat\Omega)}\le C igl(h\|u\|_{H^2(\widehat\Omega)}+\epsilon_{F,h}^{\mathrm{bulk}}+\epsilon_{\partial,h} igr).$$ where $C$ is independent of $h$. For the parabolic geometry family, $\epsilon_{\partial,h}\le C_G(e_0+e_1)\le C_Gh$.
alg-certified-convex-polygon-overlap:
## Definition

Input two finite, positive-area convex polygons $P,Q\subset\mathbb Q^2$ with rational vertices listed cyclically; output their exact rational intersection polygon and its exact area, or `unresolved` if a required orientation sign or convexity condition cannot be certified. Normalize each polygon to counterclockwise order by exact signed area. For each directed edge of $Q$, clip the current cyclic vertex list of $P$ to its closed left half-plane. Evaluate each orientation exactly: clear a common positive denominator from the rational coordinates and call [[alg-certified-dyadic-geometric-predicate]] on the resulting integer (hence dyadic) coordinates. For a crossing segment $S E$, insert the exact rational intersection $S+t(E-S)$ with $t=s(S)/(s(S)-s(E))$, where $s(X)$ is the signed edge determinant. Remove consecutive duplicate vertices after each pass. Return zero area for fewer than three noncollinear output vertices; otherwise compute the shoelace area exactly. No floating tolerance is used.
thm-certified-polygon-overlap-correctnes:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For rational positive-area convex polygons $P,Q$ whose required orientation signs are certified, [[alg-certified-convex-polygon-overlap]] terminates and returns exactly $P\cap Q$ as a cyclic rational polygon, with its exact Lebesgue area. Empty intersections and intersections consisting only of a point or segment return area zero. The result can be used as the exact weight $|P\cap Q|$ in [[def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping]].
alg-delaunay-seeded-curved-uniform-nvb-r:
## Definition

Input the exact dyadic square $[-1,1]^2$, a tolerance $0<\tau\le1/4$, and the exact shear $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$. The boundary features are the four closed edges and four vertices; features are incident when their sets intersect, and separation is the minimum Euclidean distance between nonincident feature sets. Record the interior boundary-angle certificate $\alpha=\pi/2$ and the nonincident-feature separation certificate $\sigma=1$. Run exact planar Delaunay insertion on the four square corners. Verify its output consists of two triangles sharing a diagonal; label that diagonal reference on both triangles and label the boundary edges nonreference. Set $k=0$. While $(3/2)2^{-k}(2\sqrt2)>\tau$, set $\eta_K^2=1$, $o_K^2=0$ on every current cell and call [[alg-dorfler-marking-and-conforming-nvb-refinement]] with $\theta_E=1$, $\theta_O=1$. Start the cycle budget at $B=1$; if the call returns `budget-exhausted`, retry from the unchanged mesh with $B$ doubled until it returns `complete`. A complete call requests three generations on every cell and uses recursive conformity closure; then set $k\leftarrow k+1$ and test the diameter bound again. Map every output reference triangle by the common shear $\Phi$ and return the mapped cells, feature certificates, and $k$. If a predicate is unresolved, the Delaunay seed does not have the stated two-triangle form, or closure returns invalid input, return `unresolved`.
thm-curved-uniform-nvb-quality-and-termi:
## Statement

For every tolerance $0<\tau\le\sigma/4=1/4$, the algorithm [[alg-delaunay-seeded-curved-uniform-nvb-refinement]] with square boundary angle $\alpha=\pi/2$ and nonincident-feature separation $\sigma=1$ terminates after finitely many three-generation cycles. Its reference triangles remain right isosceles with minimum angle $\pi/4$, all interfaces match, and every curved cell map is orientation preserving with mapped metric condition number at most $9/4$ times the reference-cell condition number. The returned maximum curved-cell diameter is at most $\tau$. This is a guarantee for this square/shear family; it asserts no general Delaunay minimum-angle theorem, adaptive complexity bound, or 3D shape bound.
